learningObjective: Explain what AOTInductor produces as an artifact and how it is loaded/executed at deployment.

canonicalClaims.claim: AOTInductor takes an ExportedProgram, runs the Inductor compilation stack ahead of time, and produces a shared library (.so) containing the compiled kernels plus a small runtime wrapper; the artifact can be loaded and executed from C++ or Python without re-running torch.compile.
nonImplications: Does not imply AOTInductor supports every op that torch.compile does.
Does not imply the .so is architecture-portable; it targets the compile-time hardware/OS.

misconceptions.claim: AOTInductor is a runtime JIT and re-compiles per process.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It compiles ahead of time and produces a reusable native artifact.

misconceptions.claim: AOTInductor artifacts are Python pickles requiring the full PyTorch install.
misconceptions.whyWrong: They are native shared libraries loadable from C++.

misconceptions.claim: AOTInductor only rewrites the FX graph and returns nothing executable.
AOTInductor artifacts are architecture-portable across CPU/GPU vendors.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The artifact targets the compile-time hardware; deployment must match.

implementationFacts: Produces a shared library with the compiled kernels and a wrapper for input/output marshaling
Loadable from C++ or Python; no Python source at runtime is required
performanceScenarios: AOTInductor eliminates per-process compile latency for the compiled subgraph, which is a common cold-start bottleneck for torch.compile.
